question: If Alice wants to play croquet with the Queen today, what does she say has not happened to her yet?
expected_answer: She has not been invited yet.
evidence_quote: “I should like it very much,” said Alice, “but I haven’t been invited yet.”

question: In Chapter VIII - The Queen’s Croquet-Ground, why are the three gardeners painting the white roses red?
expected_answer: They accidentally put in a white rose-tree instead of a red one and fear the Queen will have their heads cut off.
evidence_quote: this here ought to have been a _red_ rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off

question: In Chapter XI - Who Stole the Tarts?, what explanation does the Hatter give when the King calls his hat stolen?
expected_answer: He keeps hats to sell and has none of his own; he is a hatter.
evidence_quote: “I keep them to sell,” the Hatter added as an explanation; “I’ve none of my own. I’m a hatter.”
